note: Axiom is consumer-neutral: these scenarios are consumer use cases mapped to generic identity contracts. Run results are in docs/operations/axiom-integration-scenario-ledger.md and evidence/last-run.json; 'evidence_level' here is the kind of evidence, not a pass claim.

scenarios.title: The agent acts for a person
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Workforce login, authorized delegation, subject/actor preservation, source-application binding, downstream audience and scope limits.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Gateway policy and dispatch.
scenarios.axiom_profile: RFC 8693 on-behalf-of (Axiom profile: subject_token only, act = authenticated workload)

scenarios.title: The agent acts for a customer
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: CIAM identity, bounded consent, permitted downstream continuation, wrong customer/purpose/resource denial and withdrawal.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Customer application UI and business execution.
scenarios.axiom_profile: Customer consent grant + RFC 8693 delegated token (terminal)

scenarios.title: A scheduled agent runs without a person
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Workload authentication and issuance without human authority; expiry, permitted destinations and inactive-client denial.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Scheduler and job execution.
scenarios.axiom_profile: client_credentials (client_secret_basic) + explicit exchange edges

scenarios.title: Agents calling agents
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Client A to broker to client B to resource under the agreed exchange profile; wrong recipient, actor substitution, widening and excessive depth denied.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Agent coordination and transport.
scenarios.axiom_profile: RFC 8693 chain through a registered intermediary; depth bounded by explicit edges

scenarios.title: The agent calling tools and systems
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Distinct resource audiences, permitted scope sets and token-type checks through generic receiver fixtures.
scenarios.outside_axiom: MCP/tool authorization and real tool effects.
scenarios.axiom_profile: RESOURCE edges; terminal resource tokens; receiver fixture

scenarios.title: The agent talking to the AI model
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: The applicable identity token and status contract, including a status check when no new exchange is needed. Never put a provider key in Axiom token evidence.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Model keys, model dispatch, metering and budgets.
scenarios.axiom_profile: RFC 7662 introspection as status check without a new exchange

scenarios.title: Proving the agent is who it claims to be
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Authenticate the workload using the selected supported profile; reject impersonation and replay where the profile promises it. Separate client authentication from sender-constrained access tokens.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Receiver enforcement of a selected sender constraint.
scenarios.axiom_profile: client_secret_basic only; no private_key_jwt/mTLS/DPoP
open_decisions: D-S07 workload proof and sender-constraint profile

scenarios.title: Crossing boundaries
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Selected issuer/trust profile, signed subject/actor evidence, issuer/audience/replay checks and explicit refusal of untrusted issuers.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Partner integration and partner policy.
scenarios.axiom_profile: none selected

scenarios.title: A user logs out while agents are still working
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Successful logout revokes the intended durable authority; affected exchange/introspection denies and independent sessions follow the documented policy.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Consumer frequency of status checking and stopping active work.
scenarios.axiom_profile: OIDC RP-Initiated Logout (POST) ends the durable session; derived tokens inactive online

scenarios.title: A human in the loop and a record afterwards
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: If the existing optional approved-action issuance profile is retained, test that it accepts only authenticated, bounded approval evidence and cannot be widened through token issuance. Do not make business-field interpretation a generic IdP requirement.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Approval UI, exact business-action canonicalization, approval decision, workflow and receiver idempotency.
scenarios.axiom_profile: Axiom approved-action issuance profile (Phase 3.8; ActionApprovalIT, ApprovedActionUseTimeIT, IssuanceCommitBoundaryIT)
scenarios.evidence_level: Java IT evidence only (no Python contract)

scenarios.title: An agent misbehaves halfway through a request
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Revoke the applicable client, grant, token or supported opaque context and prevent reissuance from revoked authority. Test independent grants remain usable.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Misbehavior detection, business branch relationships and cancelling running compute.
scenarios.axiom_profile: session/grant/client/workload revocation re-checked at exchange and introspection

scenarios.title: Long-running work
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Valid renewal/resume authority survives the agreed restart; expired credentials alone cannot renew; cancelled grants cannot revive.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Durable workflow execution and callback processing.
scenarios.axiom_profile: standing grant renewal handle with rotation and reuse revocation
scenarios.evidence_level: issuer contract executed; restart survival and non-revival exercised in the opt-in disruptive test

scenarios.title: Acting for a person who is not there
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Explicit, bounded standing consent/renewal authority; wrong client and expired/withdrawn authority denied without requiring an interactive user at every call.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Scheduling and business approval collection.
scenarios.axiom_profile: standing grant (explicit, bounded, withdrawable)

scenarios.title: One agent serving many people
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Concurrent calls from one workload client for two subjects and tenants with distinct grants; prevent subject, grant, context and token mix-ups. Test selective revocation.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Agent memory, result and cache isolation.
scenarios.axiom_profile: per-subject exchange keyed by sub + sid/delegation_id + tenant_id; tenant-scoped clients
scenarios.evidence_level: issuer contract executed: 60 concurrent exchanges by workloads in two tenants (two people, three customers) with zero subject/grant/tenant mix-ups, 10 concurrent cross-tenant exchange attempts refused, cross-tenant introspection active=false, selective revocation. A single client spanning two tenants does not exist in Axiom (clients are tenant-scoped), so that literal form is not applicable rather than proven.

scenarios.title: An agent for a team, not a person
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Actual group/membership/role and accountable service-identity contracts; membership removal affects only the authority it governs. Do not invent a team subject from client credentials.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Agent ownership reviews and team governance.
scenarios.axiom_profile: application roles/memberships; teams grant nothing by themselves

scenarios.title: An outside company's agent asks to check an order
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Selected partner assertion/client trust, mapping and narrow issuance; wrong issuer, partner, audience and revoked trust denied.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Partner onboarding agreement and order authorization.
scenarios.axiom_profile: none selected

scenarios.title: Agents on platforms you do not control
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Selected external workload identity verification and mapping, separate from represented human/customer authority; reject fake or replayed assertions.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Hosting platform and its identity issuance.
scenarios.axiom_profile: workload-federation client assertion framework present; no provider profile configured
open_decisions: D-S17 external workload identity provider profile

scenarios.title: Stronger proof for sensitive steps
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Verify trusted authentication strength/freshness and preserve permitted assurance through exchange. Reject caller-written assurance and stale authentication. Label stub upstream evidence; native MFA/passkeys remain deferred.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Real external MFA ceremony and sensitive-operation enforcement.
scenarios.axiom_profile: acr=urn:openwolf:axiom:acr:pwd, amr=[pwd], auth_time on interactive login; preserved through exchange; caller-supplied acr ignored
scenarios.evidence_level: issuer contract executed for password assurance

scenarios.title: The agent is tricked, not hacked
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Tokens stay within the authorized audience/scope/grant ceiling; malicious requests cannot turn read authority into write authority. Agent-authored text is not proof of permission.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Prompt-injection defenses and business-intent policy.
scenarios.axiom_profile: scope/audience/grant ceilings at issuance

scenarios.title: The life of an agent identity
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: Provision, rotate, suspend, reactivate where allowed, retire and audit a generic workload client; test old credentials and outstanding-token status without reviving retired identities.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Agent inventory, deployment and review workflow.
scenarios.axiom_profile: workload register/suspend/reactivate/retire; two-person secret rotation with overlap

scenarios.title: Break-glass
scenarios.axiom_issuer_scope: If the existing optional emergency issuance profile is retained, test authenticated grant input, narrow audience/scope, short expiry, revocation and issuer audit. Do not require a generic IdP to understand incident policy or self-approval.
scenarios.outside_axiom: Incident approval, self-approval prohibition, emergency business policy and post-incident review.
scenarios.axiom_profile: no emergency token-issuance profile in Axiom (Policy Studio break-glass is a separate policy-administration feature)
